messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: stan/demo directory?
parts:
Let me know if I can trash the files that are left
(see below).

The context is that I'm cleaning up our Git
repository in anticipation of the release.

I got rid of all the files I put in stan/src/demo,
none of which we need any more.

For the rest, most if not all of which I believe
Matt created, we either need to get rid of them
or make sure they run. Here's the list:

stan/src/demo/
experiment.hpp
isnmf.cpp
lda.cpp
model1.cpp
normal.cpp

The first four don't compile, because

src/stan/agrad/agrad_special_functions.hpp

moved to

src/stan/agrad/special_functions.hpp.

The fifth, normal.cpp, has additional problems,
which also appear to be file-renaming related.

What we're eventually going to want to do is
doc the C++ API in addition to the Stan
programming language. It seems to me that'd
be a natural point at which to include these
things.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan/demo directory?
parts:
Thanks. I just pushed the deletes.

I left the demo targets in makefile and also
the make/demo file with the actual instructions.
Thus if you have

src/demo/foo.cpp

you can make it with

make demo/foo

and the executable will be built as

demo/foo

- Bob
